title: Local testing under a sign twist
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $T$ be a nonadaptive tester for functions $\Omega\to\{-1,1\}$, let $P$ be a property of such functions, and let $\rho$ be a real rate. For any fixed function $\phi:\Omega\to\{-1,1\}$, if $T$ locally tests $P$ with rate $\rho$, then the tester that multiplies each queried answer by $\phi$ locally tests the property consisting of functions $f$ for which the pointwise product $\phi f$ satisfies $P$, with the same rate $\rho$.
hypotheses_covered: $T$ is a nonadaptive tester from $\Omega$ to the signs, with $r$ query positions
$P$ is a property of sign-valued functions on $\Omega$
$T$ is a local tester for $P$ with rate $\rho$
